headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and clipboard interaction: Windsurf can read/write local workspace state while the zoomcamp profile provides no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files, use clipboard, and consume MCP/server content, so attacker-controlled text in shared files could influence its tool use. The zoomcamp profile is a docs-only course repo with no runtime isolation or parser protections, so if its materials are copied into Windsurf, prompt injection is plausible. The pairwise bridge is indirect but real.
conditions: IF content from the zoomcamp repo is copied into Windsurf or opened in its workspace
IF Windsurf treats file or clipboard text as instructions during Cascade tool use
mitigations: Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Keep course materials in a read-only folder
Avoid pasting untrusted repo text into agent prompts
Use a separate workspace for the zoomcamp repo
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-fed instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: The zoomcamp profile is open-source and does not indicate sensitive data, but Windsurf reads workspace files and has broad network egress, so any sensitive local files in the shared workspace could be exposed to its backend or external services. Because the pair shares local filesystem state via Windsurf's concurrency model, leakage is plausible in default use, though the blast radius depends on what is stored locally.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the same local workspace as Windsurf
IF Windsurf uploads file contents or context to its model proxy or MCP-connected services
mitigations: Do not store secrets in the shared workspace
Use a separate non-sensitive checkout for the course repo
Review Windsurf MCP connections before opening files
Turn off cloud-backed features for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via the local filesystem across instances. The zoomcamp repo is a codebase/course artifact that could be edited or cloned locally, so concurrent writes can conflict if both agents touch the same checkout. The overlap is not guaranteed, but the shared mutable workspace makes contention plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local checkout
IF Windsurf auto-edits files while another instance or process also modifies git state
mitigations: Use one writer per repository
Lock the workspace during agent runs
Commit or stash before starting Windsurf
Separate read-only and writeable clones
requires-engineering: add file-locking around agent actions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can act on generated code and modify files, so if it consumes zoomcamp-derived outputs as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into edits or commits. The zoomcamp profile is a course repo rather than a verified execution environment, so its outputs should not be treated as ground truth. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses zoomcamp-derived text as authoritative instructions or facts
IF Windsurf applies those outputs to code edits, shell commands, or git commits without verification
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Cross-check course instructions against primary docs
Disable auto-execute for generated commands
Use a verification checklist for any derived facts
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gating before actions

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or regulated data class is documented for the zoomcamp repo, while Windsurf handles local source code and open files with optional BYOK secrets. The only concrete compliance concern is that secrets or regulated data could be placed into Windsurf's workspace, but the pair itself does not show a documented mismatch. The other agent is not cited for a residency issue because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the Windsurf workspace
IF Windsurf is used in an environment with stricter retention or residency rules than the local repo
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Review Windsurf security docs before use
Use a non-sensitive demo repository
Confirm retention settings for any connected services
requires-engineering: formalize a data-classification policy
